description: Assign group names to contacts for organization and range-based selection. Groups are a fundamental organizational tool in PFC, allowing contacts to be categorized, selected, and manipulated based on group membership. Contacts can belong to multiple groups via different slots. By default, the group name is assigned to the 'Default' slot. Use 'slot' keyword to specify a particular slot. By default, only mechanical contacts are considered. IMPORTANT: The 'remove' keyword applies to ALL contacts (or a previously active range); it cannot be combined with a 'range' keyword in the same command.

methods.description: Set contact group name in a given slot

parameters.group_name: Group name to assign (string or int)

methods.description: Get contact group name from a given slot

parameters.slot: Optional slot to remove from (if None, removes from all slots)

methods.description: Get all groups this contact belongs to
methods.returns: Dictionary mapping slot names to group names

methods.description: Test if contact is in specified group

parameters.slot: Optional slot to search (if None, searches all slots)

methods.returns: True if contact is in the group

notes: Python SDK requires iteration over contacts - cannot assign group to all contacts in one call
Command interface is more efficient for bulk group assignment
Use range specification in command interface to avoid Python iteration
Python provides richer query capabilities (in_group, groups dict)

6.0: Live 6.00: the first slot is the group name (String); 'remove' and 'slot' follow the name.

The manuals list an 'add' keyword (assign s to the next available slot). The engine rejects it with 'Unused extra parameter' on 6.00, 7.00 and 9.8, after it has already assigned s to slot Default. Use 'slot <s2>' to pick another slot.
7.0: Live 7.0 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>'); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself. 'remove' and 'slot' follow the group name.
